q-29886.name: Question 1
q-29886.problem: Find the integral of $2{x}^{7/3}-\frac{1}{3x}$ with respect to $x.$
q-29886.worked_solution:
Applying the sum and constant factor rules, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int (2{x}^{7/3}-\frac{1}{3x})\text{d}x & =\int 2{x}^{7/3}\,\text{d}x-\frac{1}{3}\int \frac{1}{x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =2\cdot \frac{{x}^{7/3+1}}{(\frac{7}{3}+1)}-\frac{1}{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡|x|+C \\  & =\frac{3}{5}{x}^{10/3}-\frac{1}{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡|x|+C.\end{aligned}
$$

q-29886.html:
Question 1
?

Find the integral of 2x7/3−13x with respect to x.

a
72x2/3−ln⁡|x|+C
b
15x1/3−13ln⁡|x|+C
c
75x7/3−3ln⁡|x|+C
d
35x10/3−13ln⁡|x|+C
e
52x7/3−3ln⁡|x|+C
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Applying the sum and constant factor rules, we get

∫(2x7/3−13x)dx=∫2x7/3dx−13∫1xdx=2⋅x7/3+1(73+1)−13ln⁡|x|+C=35x10/3−13ln⁡|x|+C.

q-49067.name: Question 2
q-49067.worked_solution:
Expanding the binomial and applying the sum and constant factor rules, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int {(1+\frac{1}{x})}^{2}\text{d}x & =\int (1+\frac{2}{x}+\frac{1}{{x}^{2}})\text{d}x \\  & =\int \text{d}x+2\int \frac{1}{x}\,\text{d}x+\int \frac{1}{{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =x+2\operatorname{ln}⁡|x|+\frac{{x}^{-2+1}}{-2+1}+C \\  & =x+2\operatorname{ln}⁡|x|-\frac{1}{x}+C.\end{aligned}
$$

Lastly, let's rewrite the constant so that we can combine it with the natural logarithm. For any constant $C,$ we can always write $C=2\operatorname{ln}⁡K$ where $K$ is some other positive constant. Doing this allows us to combine the constant with $2\operatorname{ln}⁡|x|$ term, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int {(1+\frac{1}{x})}^{2}\text{d}x & =x-\frac{1}{x}+2\operatorname{ln}⁡|x|+2\operatorname{ln}⁡K \\  & =x-\frac{1}{x}+2(\operatorname{ln}⁡|x|+\operatorname{ln}⁡K) \\  & =x-\frac{1}{x}+2\operatorname{ln}⁡(K|x|).\end{aligned}
$$

q-49067.html:
Question 2
?

What is the antiderivative of (1+1x)2?

a
1−1x+2ln⁡(|K|x)
b
x−1x+2ln⁡(K|x|)
c
1+2ln⁡(|K|x)
d
x+(1+ln⁡(K|x|))2
e
x−1x+ln⁡(2K|x|)
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Expanding the binomial and applying the sum and constant factor rules, we get

∫(1+1x)2dx=∫(1+2x+1x2)dx=∫dx+2∫1xdx+∫1x2dx=x+2ln⁡|x|+x−2+1−2+1+C=x+2ln⁡|x|−1x+C.

Lastly, let's rewrite the constant so that we can combine it with the natural logarithm. For any constant C, we can always write C=2ln⁡K where K is some other positive constant. Doing this allows us to combine the constant with 2ln⁡|x| term, and we get

∫(1+1x)2dx=x−1x+2ln⁡|x|+2ln⁡K=x−1x+2(ln⁡|x|+ln⁡K)=x−1x+2ln⁡(K|x|).

q-103373.name: Question 3
q-103373.problem: Find the integral of $\frac{2}{x}+3{x}^{2}$ with respect to $x.$
q-103373.worked_solution:
Applying the sum and constant factor rules, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int (\frac{2}{x}+3{x}^{2})\text{d}x & =2\int \frac{1}{x}\,\text{d}x+3\int {x}^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =2\operatorname{ln}⁡|x|+{x}^{3}+C.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 3
?

Find the integral of 2x+3x2 with respect to x.

a
ln⁡|x|+x3+C
b
3ln⁡|x|+2x3+C
c
3ln⁡|x|+3x3+C
d
2ln⁡|x|+3x2+C
e
2ln⁡|x|+x3+C
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Applying the sum and constant factor rules, we get

∫(2x+3x2)dx=2∫1xdx+3∫x2dx=2ln⁡|x|+x3+C.
